full_judgment:
7. The defendant Nos. 2 to 4 contested the suit denying all material allegations, inter alia, stating that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and that the suit is barred by limitation. 

 2. Is the suit barred by limitation? 

 15. Mr. M.A. Samad, the learned Advocate for the appellant submits that the suit is not maintainable in its present form. Admittedly the plaintiff claims in the alternative a specific amount of money and hence its first prayer for specific enforcement of contract cannot be maintainable. The suit is barred by limitation as the plaintiff has not been filed the suit within time. He further submits that Chief Executive of the Mills or others have not removed the stock in trade or other current assets. It is further stated that since the enterprise was in running condition before and after the advertisement of Disinvestment Board, all kinds of transactions were normal. The Disinvestment Board in its meeting held on 08.09.1977 under the Chairmanship of the then Advisor to President in Charge of the Ministry of Industries, considered the representation for replacement of the current assets of the Mills and decided that no reduction shall be made on account of current assets depletion and the Board further considered that out of Taka 6,07,000.00 shown as insurance claim pending in the inventory report as mentioned at serial No. 10 of paragraph-7 of the plaint Taka 5,81,487.55 had already been realised on 04.07.1977 by defendant No.4. The Board therefore, decided to allow reduction of the offered price by Taka 5,81,487.55. The member secretary of Disinvestment Board in its letter dated 03.10.1977 informed the plaintiff about the Disinvestment Board's decision for reduction of Taka 5,81,487.55 from the original offer of Taka 39,00,000.00 and that no reduction shall be allowed on account of current assets depletion. The plaintiff signed the deed of agreement for sale of the unit on 11.10.1977, after signing of agreement, the plaintiff had nothing to say.
